title: The Prize for the Best Improvement
title_ja: 最も成長した人への賞
fact_notes: 人物・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例。実在の研究結果や統計を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional community art program planned to recognize participants at the end of a six-week course.
sentences.ja: 架空の地域芸術プログラムは6週間の講座の終わりに参加者を表彰する計画を立てた。

sentences.en: The organizers first suggested awarding a prize to the person whose final painting received the highest score from the instructors.
sentences.ja: 主催者は当初、最終作品が指導者から最高点を得た人に賞を贈る案を出した。

sentences.en: One volunteer questioned whether this approach would adequately recognize the achievements of beginners.
sentences.ja: あるボランティアはこの方法が初心者の成果を十分評価するか疑問を示した。

sentences.en: Some participants had entered the course with considerable experience, whereas others had never painted before.
sentences.ja: かなりの経験を持って参加した人もいれば初めて絵を描く人もいた。

sentences.en: The organizers then considered offering an award for the greatest improvement instead.
sentences.ja: そこで代わりに最も成長した人への賞を考えた。

sentences.en: They compared each person's early work with a painting completed at the end of the course.
sentences.ja: 各人の初期の作品と講座終了時の作品を比較した。

sentences.en: However, they discovered that improvement was difficult to summarize using a single numerical score.
sentences.ja: しかし成長を一つの数値で要約するのは難しいと分かった。

sentences.en: One participant had developed greater technical accuracy, while another had gained the confidence to experiment independently.
sentences.ja: 技術的正確さを伸ばした人もいれば自力で試す自信を得た人もいた。

sentences.en: Rather than choosing between the two awards immediately, the organizers examined what they wanted the recognition to accomplish.
sentences.ja: 二種類の賞からすぐ選ぶのでなく表彰で何を達成したいか検討した。

sentences.en: They agreed that the course was intended to encourage learning and creative exploration, not merely to identify the most skilled painter.
sentences.ja: 講座は最も技能のある画家を見つけるだけでなく学習と創造的探究を促す目的だと合意した。

sentences.en: They therefore invited each participant to display two works together with a short explanation of a personal learning goal.
sentences.ja: そこで各参加者に二作品と個人の学習目標の短い説明を展示するよう促した。

sentences.en: The instructors provided specific comments about progress rather than ranking every achievement on the same scale.
sentences.ja: 指導者は全成果を同じ尺度で順位づけせず進捗について具体的な意見を与えた。

sentences.en: Some participants still preferred the idea of a traditional competition with a clear winner.
sentences.ja: 明確な勝者のいる従来型コンテストを好む参加者もいた。

sentences.en: The organizers listened to these views and acknowledged that competitive events could serve a different purpose.
sentences.ja: 主催者は意見を聞き競争型行事が別の目的に役立つことも認めた。

sentences.en: They explained that this particular exhibition was designed to make diverse kinds of learning visible.
sentences.ja: この展示は多様な学びを見えるように設計したと説明した。

sentences.en: For a future competition, they would establish and communicate its evaluation criteria before participants began working.
sentences.ja: 将来のコンテストでは作業開始前に評価基準を設定し伝えることにした。

sentences.en: The example illustrates that a fair evaluation depends partly on the purpose for which it is conducted.
sentences.ja: この例は公正な評価が実施目的にも左右されることを示す。

sentences.en: A measure suitable for identifying the strongest final performance may not capture every kind of individual growth.
sentences.ja: 最も優れた最終成果を特定する尺度が個人のあらゆる成長を捉えるとは限らない。

sentences.en: Recognizing different achievements need not require denying differences in skill.
sentences.ja: 異なる成果を認めることは技能差を否定する必要はない。

sentences.en: It requires clarity about what is being valued and why that particular standard has been chosen.
sentences.ja: 何を評価しなぜその基準を選んだかを明確にする必要がある。

vocabulary.definition: people living in a particular area
people taking part in an activity
the act of trying to discover something
a system used to compare values
the quality of being easy to understand

questions.prompt: What was the original prize based on?
options: The greatest attendance at other events.
The cost of the materials alone.

questions.prompt: Why did the volunteer question the plan?
options: Everyone had the same amount of experience.
The organizers had no paintings to judge.
Beginners had already won every prize.
questions.explanation_ja: 開始時の経験が異なった。

questions.prompt: What alternative award did they consider?
options: A prize for the oldest participant.
A prize for the greatest improvement.
A prize for collecting the most money.
A prize for choosing the largest canvas.
questions.explanation_ja: 最も成長した人への賞。

questions.prompt: Why was one numerical improvement score difficult?
options: Every participant had produced identical work.
The instructors refused to observe progress.
The program had no final paintings.
questions.explanation_ja: 成長には異なる側面があった。

questions.prompt: What goal did the organizers identify?
options: Sell every painting for the highest price.
questions.explanation_ja: 学習と創造的探究を促す。

options: Two works and an explanation of a personal goal.
A list of other people's scores.
questions.explanation_ja: 二作品と個人目標の説明。

questions.prompt: What did some participants still prefer?
options: A traditional competition with a clear winner.
questions.explanation_ja: 明確な勝者がいる競技。

questions.prompt: Why communicate future competition criteria in advance?
options: Participants should know what the event is intended to value.
All competitions should use hidden standards.
The organizers wanted to eliminate all differences in ability.
questions.explanation_ja: 事前に評価されるものを明確にするため。

questions.prompt: What does capture mean in the second sentence?

options: Every evaluation should rank people by final performance alone.
Recognizing growth requires denying all skill differences.
Fair evaluation requires criteria matched to its purpose.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的に合った評価基準が必要。

grammar.explanation_ja: whileは対比、過去完了は以前の成長を示す。

grammar.focus: not merely to identify the most skilled painter
grammar.explanation_ja: not merelyは単に〜するだけではない。
